proseFields.Airbags: Not deployed — steering wheel centre and passenger fascia are intact in the interior photos, no deployed curtain visible, and no airbag warning lamp is visible on the illuminated cluster. Confirm A-pillar/curtain covers on inspection as a formality.
proseFields.Red Flags:
- Q-suffix windscreen sticker on a Cat S lot: this lot was entered by Copart having purchased it to resell, not by an insurer. On a Cat S this is a possible re-entry flag — it may indicate a previously-bought, re-entered-unrepaired lot (sometimes because damage proved worse than the photos, or repair was uneconomic). This is a possibility, not a verdict — innocent explanations exist — but establish why it is being sold this way before bidding, and do not bid unless that reason is known and priced in.
- V5 Status: No. On any Cat S the buyer must apply to DVLA for a replacement V5, which will be reissued permanently marked Category S and will show on all future HPI checks. With no V5 supplied here, the DVLA application is an additional administrative step and minor delay — factor it in.
- Rear structural extent unknown: the torn rear quarter/rear panel corner is visible, but how far the deformation runs into the boot floor and rear chassis corner cannot be scoped from photos. This is the single biggest cost uncertainty on the lot.
- Three separate damage zones (front, side, rear) suggest either a multi-impact event or more than one event — each zone has been assessed independently on what is visible; no single-impact narrative is assumed.
- MOT not valid and vehicle untaxed — full retest required before road use; recent history flags front tyres near the legal limit.
proseFields.Bidder Note: A desirable, genuine-mileage (41,716 miles, MOT-corroborated), running and driving manual Civic Sport Line with moderate three-zone damage — but the rear corner is structural, the V5 is absent, and the Q-suffix entry means you must establish why this lot is being resold before committing money.

proseFields.Confidence Level: Medium — good photo coverage of all three damage zones and a legible dash, but the rear structural depth, headlamp serviceability, and cooling pack condition are all unconfirmable remotely, and the Q-suffix provenance question is unresolved.
proseFields.Key Cost Drivers:
1. The rear corner structural repair (torn quarter and deformed rear panel) — this is welded-panel work requiring a bodyshop with jig/measuring capability, and it drives both the labour bill and the Cat S classification.
2. Two headlamps whose serviceability cannot be confirmed — if both need replacement, even at breakers' prices, this is a material line.
3. The car is damaged at three zones (front, side, rear), so paint and blend labour spans most of the car despite each individual zone being moderate.
proseFields.Exit Band Position: mid-low — desirable spec and genuine low mileage, but confirmed rear structural damage across a three-zone Cat S with no V5 supplied.
proseFields.Margin Calculation: The repair is moderate-to-heavy in character: the front and side zones are bolt-on and panel-repair work, but the rear corner requires welded structural repair and refinishing spans most of the car, so labour and paint dominate the itemised total alongside the two precautionary headlamp lines. The exit sits at the mid-low step of the Cat S band — the spec and mileage are strong sellers, but the structural marker, three-zone history, and V5 absence cap what a realistic buyer pays. The margin picture therefore hinges on two things the photos cannot resolve: whether the rear structure is shallow (in which case the repair lands at or under the itemised total and the deal works at a sensible hammer price) and whether both headlamps survive (worst case adds real money). The Q-suffix re-entry question is the gating risk — if a previous buyer walked away from this car, your bid ceiling should assume their reason was cost. Keep the hammer price disciplined against the code-computed margin table, and treat the itemised total as a floor, not a final figure, until the rear structure is verified.
proseFields.Recommended Action: Book a £10 Copart WhatsApp video inspection (minimum 48hrs before sale). The rear structural depth and front lamp/cooling pack condition are exactly the unknowns a video walk-around can narrow — see checklist below. Do not bid blind on this one given the Q-suffix provenance question and the unscoped rear structure.
proseFields.Realistic Exit Value: Reference context from the live market data (June 2026, calibrated to the Copart-listed 41,716 miles): retail £12,103 / £12,699 / £13,312 (low/average/high) and trade £9,574 / £10,121 / £10,691 (low/average/high). Desirability signals are genuinely good: sought-after Sport Line trim, manual petrol turbo, low mileage for a 2019 car, clean tidy interior, and a cleanly ascending MOT mileage ladder. Against that: this is a Cat S with confirmed structural damage at the rear corner, damage across three zones, no V5 supplied, and a Q-suffix provenance that a diligent retail buyer's HPI/salvage-record search will surface alongside the permanent Cat S marker. The damage is moderate overall (front and side are cosmetic; rear is structural but localised to one corner), which would normally sit mid-band, but the structural element plus the missing V5 and provenance question pull it down a step within the Cat S band.
proseFields.Visible Damage Summary:
Confirmed body style: 5-door Hatchback (rear doors and rear quarter visible in side photos; rear cabin shot confirms rear seating row and rear door). 2019 Honda Civic 1.0 VTEC Turbo 126 Sport Line, manual 6-speed (gear knob confirms), RHD confirmed from interior shots. Windscreen sticker suffix: Q — this lot was purchased by Copart to resell, not entered by an insurer. This carries two implications addressed in Red Flags below.

The vehicle has three distinct damage zones:

1. Front end — impact damage, low-to-mid strike height. The upper bumper/grille assembly is broken across the full width of the front: the grille surround and upper bumper trim are fractured and displaced, the radiator/condenser pack is exposed to view, and the bumper-to-wing junctions are detached at both front corners with the wheel-arch liner hanging at one corner. The front lower splitter/lip is damaged with sections broken through. Both headlamps are present with lenses appearing intact, but their mounting tabs and brackets cannot be confirmed — the surrounding trim is broken and the bumper is displaced on both sides, so serviceability of either lamp cannot be confirmed from the photos. Both front fog lamps appear present and intact in their recesses (each checked individually). The bonnet appears largely straight in the three-quarter shots, but the leading edge near the grille cannot be fully cleared from the close-up — flagged below. The radiator/condenser pack is visible and exposed; no fluid is seen escaping any component and no deformation is clearly visible on the pack itself — condition unconfirmed, flagged below. Engine bay otherwise appears undisturbed; no visible deformation to the suspension towers or visible structure.

2. Side — impact damage, low strike height. A run of dents along the bottom edges of both the front door and rear door on one side, at the sill/skirt line, with the side skirt trim scuffed and cracked. The opposite flank appears undamaged in the photos. This is a 5-door — the front door, rear door, and side skirt are accounted as separate items.

3. Rear end — impact damage, low-to-mid strike height, concentrated at one rear corner. The rear bumper has been removed/displaced (shown detached in the corner close-up), the rear quarter panel's lower rear section is crushed and torn with bare metal exposed, and the rear panel/bumper mounting structure at that corner is deformed. Parking-sensor wiring hangs loose at the corner. Both rear lamp clusters were checked individually and both appear intact in the photos. The torn rear quarter/rear panel corner is the most plausible trigger for the Cat S classification — structural intrusion at the rear corner behind the bumper line. This is a hypothesis to confirm on inspection, not a certainty.

Dashboard photo: odometer reads 041,716 miles — this matches the Copart listed figure of 41,716 exactly, so the mileage can be stated confidently. Ignition-on state with engine off (0 rpm, 0 mph); a TPMS warning is illuminated, consistent with the listing's tyre history rather than a fault narrative. No airbag warning lamp visible. Copart verified the engine starts and the transmission engages (Run and Drive).

Interior: clean, no airbag deployment visible — steering wheel centre and passenger fascia intact, no curtain deployment visible on the visible trim. Roof panel undamaged.

MOT/mileage corroboration: the DVSA MOT ladder runs cleanly 17,397 → 17,702 → 25,112 → 37,605 miles (Aug 2022 to Apr 2025), consistent with the current 41,716 — no rollback or implausible jump detected. This is positive reassurance the mileage is genuine, which matters on a non-insurer-entered (Q-suffix) lot. One damage-relevant advisory: "Offside Front Lower bumper skirt slightly insecure" was noted at both tests in April 2024; the subsequent April 2025 test was clean in that area — likely addressed. DVSA fact only; confirm repair documentation was obtained if it concerns you, but the later clean test softens this considerably.

One or both front wheels show rim scuffing/kerb marks on the spokes (corner attribution uncertain from the photos — hedged accordingly); refurbishment budgeted for one wheel, verify both on inspection.

MOT status: Not valid; vehicle untaxed — a fresh MOT will be required as part of return-to-road.
proseFields.Alternative Damage Scenario: Primary damage is listed as "Unknown" with Front End / Rear End / Side as secondary and additional descriptors — the photos corroborate all three zones, so the listing and photos are broadly consistent. The most probable mundane read is a road traffic incident involving a rear corner strike (the structural trigger) with the front and side damage either from the same multi-vehicle event or a separate low-speed incident. The front damage is largely cosmetic/clip-on (bumper, grille, splitter); if the rear structure proves shallow on inspection, this lot is lighter than the Cat S label suggests — conversely, if the boot floor is involved, the repair escalates.
proseFields.WhatsApp Inspection Checklist:
1. Show the boot floor/load floor from inside the boot, with the carpet lifted — looking for ripples, kinks, or distortion running forward from the damaged rear corner (this determines how deep the Cat S structural damage goes).
2. Show the damaged rear corner close up from behind and below — the torn quarter section, the rear panel, and the rear chassis leg/crash-bar mounting behind the removed bumper.
3. Show both front headlamps close up from above with the bonnet open — confirm whether the mounting tabs/brackets are intact and whether either lamp is loose, cracked, or has internal damage.
4. Show the exposed radiator/condenser pack close up through the broken grille — confirm no fin crush, kinked pipes, or leak staining.
5. Confirm the bonnet opens, closes, and latches correctly, and show the leading edge and panel gaps to the wings for alignment.
6. With the keys present, start the engine and attempt to engage drive (1st and reverse) and roll the car a short distance — corroborating the Run and Drive designation at collection-readiness level.
7. Open and close both doors on the damaged side — confirm they latch and seal correctly given the dents along their lower edges.
8. Show all four tyres' tread close up — recent MOT history flags front tyres near the legal limit; confirm what is on the car now.
9. Inspect the opposite-side front headlamp — on a full-width frontal impact both lamps are implicated; check for displacement, cracking, or moisture ingress and confirm serviceability. Budget ~£150 if replacement needed — flagged as inspection allowance, not included in repair total.
10. Inspect and photograph all four wheels and tyres close-up — confirm no shredding, kerbing, cuts or bulges (the listing photos do not show the wheels clearly enough to confirm condition)
